newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close higher on red chip fever, Wall St.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close higher on red chip fever, Wall St.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended sharply higher on Monday, boosted by red chip euphoria and positive overseas trends, but brokers warned worries about the local property market could produce more volatility ahead.
"This is a rebound coming on the back of last week's oversold position, the Dow's rally and expectation of steady or lower interest rates," said Peter Lui at NAVA SC Securities.
The Hang Seng Index closed 282.05 points or 2.00 percent higher at 14,394.60, off the day's high of 14,426.55, in broad-based activity.
Turnover was a robust HK$15.30 billion, though slightly lower than Friday's HK$15.40 billion.
The Dow Industrials advanced to a new all-time high of 7,799.68 on Friday before ending at 7,782.04, its sixth consecutive record close.
Recent U.S. economic reports showing subdued inflationary forces have eased market fears of another interest rate hike in July or September, Lui said.
"Hong Kong is in a position for a rally to retest 15,000 soon," he said.
But others were not as confident.
"Until political uncertainty overhanging property stocks lifts, it will be difficult for those shares to bring the index to new highs," said Chris Geiger, associate director at Vickers Ballas.
"I think we may find ourselves stuck in a range of 14,000 to 15,000," Geiger added.
The index fell more than 500 points last week on fears that the government would impose measures to curb spiralling property prices, including issuing new guidelines to banks on mortgage lending.
The utility sector led the market, followed by the commercial and industrial sector. Hong Kong Telecom rose HK$0.55 to HK$16.90 and China Lightjumped HK$1.00 to HK$43.30.
Hutchison Whampoa put on HK$1.50 to HK$62.25 on turnover of HK$201.15 million.

The Hang Seng China-affiliated Corporations Index of 32 red chips debuted at 2,732.85. The index, which was backdated to January 4, 1993 with a base date of 1,000, gained 194.60 points, or 7.28 percent, to close at 2,867.32.
China Merchants Hai Hong added HK$1.35 to HK$16.60.
